title: Oren Cass & Noah Smith Debate the True Impact of Tariffs

reader_summary.headline: The question is, does free trade with China advance free markets or does it distort and wreck our free market?
reader_summary.overview: The question is, does free trade with China advance free markets or does it distort and wreck our free market? We have treated free trade as the natural extension of free markets. If you attempt to be for free trade with a non-market economy, you are not actually advancing free markets in any significant way at all.

key_points.text: China is pretty much the only competitive threat we face, which all our allies are facing at the same time.
key_points.evidence_quote: China is pretty much the only competitive threat we face, which all our allies are facing at the same time, and we're fighting with our allies instead of pooling our resources to stand up to China.

key_points.text: At the end of the day, if the goal is not to make America the assembly hub of the world, but actually re-industrialize.
key_points.evidence_quote: At the end of the day, if the goal is not to make America the assembly hub of the world, but actually re-industrialize, you have to actually create incentives to bring back those intermediate supplies.

key_points.text: The US is rethinking its economic playbook on tariffs, trade, manufacturing, and what it really means to support family, community, and industry.
key_points.evidence_quote: The US is rethinking its economic playbook on tariffs, trade, manufacturing, and what it really means to support family, community, and industry.

thesis: The debate centers on whether free trade with non-market economies like China advances free markets or distorts them by hindering re-industrialization and failing to address national security and family stability. The speakers argue that traditional economic models based on comparative advantage are insufficient for modern manufactured goods, which depend on policy choices rather than natural endowments, and that the US must rethink its economic playbook to support family, community, and industry beyond mere corporate profit maximization.
